title: Reserve contract lifecycle, operator UI and emergency failover playbook for Dedicated
creator: Priya Sharma
description: PRD defining the lifecycle model for Dedicated reserved capacity contracts, the operator-facing UI and APIs needed to manage contract state, and a runbook / playbook for emergency failover and preemptive actions. Focus on safe autoscale interactions, clear billing reconciliation, and auditability for regulated customers.
goals: Define canonical states for a reserve contract (Draft, Active, Top-up Pending, Replenished, Expiring, Suspended, Terminated)
Provide operator UI & API to view, simulate and perform lifecycle transitions with RBAC and audit logs
Formalize autoscale interactions so Reserved pools can safely burst into transient capacity and be preempted with deterministic rules
Document an ops playbook for emergency reclaim, tenant fencing and rapid rollback that on-call can follow during capacity incidents
Ensure billing events align to contract lifecycle transitions and provide reconciliations for customers
non_goals: Implementing a fully automated contract-negotiation flow (out of scope; migration and manual top-ups only)
Changing core scheduler architecture; we will integrate with existing runtime hooks rather than redesign scheduling internals
Replacing existing dedicated billing system — we will add reconciliation events but not change invoicing cadence
requirements: R1: Contract model in control plane with the following fields as string-typed keys: contract_id, owner_id, capacity_units, start_date, end_date, auto_refill_threshold_pct, preemption_policy_id, status
R2: Operator UI: Reserve Contracts page with filter by status/owner/region and detail view showing headroom timeline and recent bursts
R3: API endpoints: GET /contracts, GET /contracts/{id}, POST /contracts/{id}/topup, POST /contracts/{id}/suspend, POST /contracts/{id}/terminate
R4: Simulation endpoint: API + UI simulation that shows effect of preemption rule on active jobs for a given timestamp and target reclaim percentage
R5: Autoscale contract hooks: autoscaler must consult contract state and auto_refill setting before moving capacity from on-demand to reserved; documented fallback behavior when reserve is exhausted
R6: Audit logs emitted for every lifecycle change with actor, timestamp, prior_state, new_state and rationale; logs retained per compliance policy
R7: Billing events: emit structured events for start/top-up/expire/terminate mapped to billing pipeline (event schema provided in links)
R8: RBAC: only users with "contract-admin" or "sre-ops" roles can perform suspend/terminate/topup via console/API; UI must hide buttons otherwise
R9: Acceptance tests that run a simulated burst and verify fallback to designated fallback model variant and latency SLOs for non-impacted tenants remain within thresholds
R10: Playbook content: documented step-by-step operator actions for emergency reclaim, canary termination, safe rollback and customer communication templates
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Contract model exists in control plane and GET endpoints return fields described in R1 for 95% of test contracts
AC2: Console: Reserve Contracts page implemented with filters, detail drawer and action buttons; UI passes accessibility checks and UX review (design sign-off recorded)
AC3: API: POST /contracts/{id}/topup increases capacity_units and emits billing event; tests validate event received by mock billing sink

AC4: Autoscale integration: when reserve capacity is below auto_refill_threshold_pct and auto_refill=true, autoscaler triggers top-up flow and logs an action; if top-up fails, autoscaler will route new requests to fallback pool with correct metrics emitted
AC5: Simulation: running simulation for a contract returns a deterministic preemption plan and a visualization; operator validates plan in staging for two sample tenants
AC6: Audit: for 100 lifecycle transitions in staging, audit log entries are present with correct actor/rationale and immutable IDs
AC7: RBAC: attempts to call suspend/terminate/topup by an unprivileged user return 403 and no state change
AC8: Playbook validation: on-call runs scenario-based drill during the release window and succeeds in reclaiming 30% capacity within SLA without data loss; drill notes are uploaded to Confluence
AC9: Billing alignment: reconcile scheduled billing events for start/top-up/termination for two customers in staging and match expected invoiceable units
AC10: Metrics: no regression in 95th latency percentile for hosted tier when fallback routing is exercised during tests
success_metrics: SM1: Reduction in unplanned tenant preemptions by 60% within 4 weeks of GA
SM2: Mean time to restore reserved capacity after emergency reclaim < 12 minutes in drills
SM3: Operator error rate on contract transitions < 0.5% after training and UI improvements
SM4: Billing reconciliation mismatches < 0.1% for test customers in the first billing cycle
SM5: Customer satisfaction (NPS subset) improvement for dedicated customers referencing clearer contract controls
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Staging): Implement contract model and minimal API; provide CLI tools for ops to create/test contracts (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Internal Beta): Console Reserve Contracts page + simulation mode; run three tabletop drills with SRE and Solutions Engineers (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (Selective GA): Offer feature to a small cohort of Dedicated customers, enable billing events; collect telemetry and adjust preemption thresholds (3 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): Open to all Dedicated tenants, publish docs and run onboarding webinars; enable automated autoscale top-ups by default for existing contracts
Phase 5 (Post-GA): 30-day operational review and iterate on preemption policies, UI affordances and billing mapping
ops_playbook: Detect: dashboard alert (reserved-pool-headroom) triggers when headroom < 20% sustained for 5 minutes; pager duty to SRE on-call
Assess: pull contract detail; run simulation to estimate reclaim impact and list top 10 active tenants affected
Communicate: use template 'reserved-capacity-alert' to notify customers in affected list with expected timeline
Act: if immediate reclaim required, perform POST /contracts/{id}/suspend to pause new reservations then run reclaim job with target reclaim percentage
Fallback: enable fallback routing by toggling autoscale to route to ephemeral pool; monitor latency for non-dedicated tenants
Rollback: if reclaim causes customer-visible degradation, revert via POST /contracts/{id}/replenish or cancel reclaim and initiate hotfix to increase capacity
Postmortem: update incident page with cause, actions, and lessons; schedule follow-up to adjust auto_refill_threshold_pct if needed
ui_wireframe_notes: List view: columns for contract_id, owner, region, capacity_units, used_units, headroom_pct, status, next_billing_date
Detail drawer: timeline of lifecycle events, recent bursts, preemption policy summary and simulation button
Actions: contextual menu for Top-up, Suspend, Terminate, Simulate; show confirmation modal with required justification field for suspend/terminate
Operator simulation: allow toggling time and target reclaim pct; visualize affected tenants and estimated latency impact
open_questions: Q1: What is the maximum frequency of top-ups allowed per contract before we require manual approval? (Ops/Finance decision)
Q2: Should we support partial top-ups that allocate to specific availability zones only? (affects scheduler complexity)
Q3: For customers with regulatory audit needs, do we need an immutable ledger export for audit logs? (security/compliance input)
Q4: Which preemption policy should be default for new contracts: 'graceful-shrink' (evict oldest burst) or 'priority-based' (evict lowest-priority tenants)?
